name: ml-harness
description: Workspace root. Exists so that node_modules is an ancestor of both web/ and vendor/opencode/ - see the note below.
//: The interface is vendored from OpenCode at vendor/opencode, byte-identical
to a pinned commit so that upstream diffs stay possible, and aliased to
source by Vite. But Node resolves a bare import like 'core-js/es/map/group-by'
by walking UP from the importing file looking for node_modules - and
vendor/opencode is not under web/, so web/node_modules is never on that
path. The build failed on exactly that, with the package present and
Three fixes were possible. Moving the vendored tree under web/ would have
worked but buries a licence-bearing directory inside a build output folder.
A junction from vendor/ to web/node_modules would also have worked and is
forbidden here: a worktree removal once followed one and emptied the
target. Declaring a workspace is the idiomatic answer - npm hoists to the
root, and the root IS an ancestor of both trees.
frontend/ is deliberately NOT a workspace member. It is the outgoing React
app and keeps its own install until the cutover in Phase 7.
